fields.description: The monotonic per-room sequence (CHAT-SEQ-1). Positive, allocated inside the inserting transaction, unique per (room, seq), never derived from a timestamp, never client-assigned, never reused - deletes are soft. This is the sort key for a transcript, not creation: two inserts into one room can share creation to the microsecond, and seq has no timezone.
fields.label: Sequence

fields.description: The author, when they map to an ERPNext User. DELIBERATELY NOT reqd - it was reqd in Phase 1 and Phase 2 relaxes it on purpose, before any row exists. A Google Chat member with no ERPNext account (an external participant, or a Workspace user we have not provisioned) has to be STORED, because ERPNext is the record of what was said and a mirror that silently drops the messages it cannot attribute is not a record. With reqd on, those inserts fail outright and the transcript acquires holes exactly where the conversation left the company. The rule is sender OR sender_email, NEVER neither, and ChatMessage.validate enforces exactly that pair - the Link is not merely optional, it is half of a required pair.
fields.label: Sender

fields.description: The author's Chat address when sender is empty. Fills the other half of the sender OR sender_email pair (see Sender). Data(255) rather than the varchar(140) default because an address is not bounded at 140 and a truncated address is a wrong attribution rather than a missing one. Never used to look up a User at read time: if a matching User appears later, a backfill sets sender, and until it does this column is what the UI renders. Not unique and not indexed - it is an attribute of a message, not an identity to join on.
fields.label: Sender Email

fields.description: Drives rendering and unread exclusion - a user's own Triton reply should not mark their room unread.
fields.label: Sender Kind

fields.description: The body AS AUTHORED, stored verbatim and never trusted. Sanitisation happens on the way out, in the client, using DOM APIs and never innerHTML.
fields.label: Text

fields.description: Plain-text extraction. It is what the 32,000-BYTE relay budget is measured against after UTF-8 encoding, what retrieval chunks are assembled from, and what Chat Room.last_message_preview is truncated from - so no read path ever re-parses markup.
fields.label: Text (Plain)

fields.description: The reply edge. Threading is ONE level: a reply to a reply attaches to the same root, mirroring the existing Comments App, which is why thread_root never needs recomputation.
fields.label: Parent Message

fields.description: Denormalised root, maintained in before_insert as parent.thread_root or parent.name, so the thread panel is one indexed range scan instead of a recursive walk. This pair is what survives the Google threading risk: if API-created spaces cannot be threaded at all, ERPNext still holds complete thread structure and only the Chat-side rendering is lossy.
fields.label: Thread Root

fields.description: SOFT DELETE - text is retained on the row. Google's own tombstone is content-free (showDeleted returns name, deleteTime and deletionMetadata, never the body), so if ERPNext does not keep it, nobody has it. Every read path filters is_deleted = 0 except the Phase 6 oversight endpoint, which pays for the privilege with an audit row.
fields.label: Is Deleted

fields.description: spaces/{space}/messages/{message}. Data(255) with unique on the DocField - invariant I2 made STRUCTURAL. The varchar(140) default would truncate-collide two distinct Google messages into one, which is silent message loss. Declared unique here rather than only in a patch so Frappe coerces the unset value to NULL: with the constraint added only by frappe.db.add_unique, unrelayed rows store '' and the SECOND unrelayed message in the entire table fails to insert.
fields.label: Google Chat Message Name

fields.description: spaces/{space}/threads/{thread} - the thread RESOURCE NAME, never a threadKey. threadKey is documented at up to 4000 characters, which no Frappe Data field can hold and no Frappe-emitted index can key on; storing it here would be a silent truncation at insert.
fields.label: Google Chat Thread Name

fields.description: Google Message.lastUpdateTime. The monotonic guard an inbound update is tested against, so a delayed redelivery cannot overwrite a newer edit.
fields.label: Google Chat Last Update Time

fields.description: Our client- prefixed idempotency id, derived once and stored forever. Data(64) because Google caps clientAssignedMessageId at 63 characters, lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, unique within a space - and Frappe silently raises any Data length below 64 to 64 anyway. Unique per (room, client_message_id) via patch, scoped to the room because Google's own guarantee is per-space.
fields.label: Client Message ID

fields.description: Relay bookkeeping. Every write to this field uses set_value(update_modified=False): the D6 cache watermark is (max(seq), count(*), max(modified)), so a retry that touched modified would invalidate every cached digest for the room on every attempt.
fields.label: Sync State
fields.options:
Pending
Relayed
Failed
Not Mirrored
Inbound

fields.description: Which side authored this row. Three-valued, not a boolean: Triton's replies are neither an employee's message nor a mirror of one.
fields.label: Sync Origin

fields.description: This body did not fit in Google's 32,000-byte message limit and was truncated for the relay only. The ERPNext row still holds the whole thing.
fields.label: Truncated For Relay

fields.description: §4.G. Ingested with a Google createTime OLDER than the room's current tail - this message genuinely predates messages that already hold a higher seq. seq is allocated at insert and is never renumbered (Phase 5's digest watermarks and cache keys derive from it, and ADR §G.8 makes seq the only ordering), so the transcript's seq order and its createTime order disagree on exactly these rows. This flag is how a read path knows that, how the reconciliation sweep counts what it recovered after an outage, and the signal that the inbound pipeline was behind rather than that a clock was wrong - which is what clock_skew_ms answers separately.
fields.label: Late Arrival

fields.description: §4.G instrumentation: Google's createTime minus our own receive time, in milliseconds, SIGNED. Recorded, never corrected - ordering is by seq and never by a timestamp, so a skewed clock must not be allowed to move a message. Its value is as a trend: Google returns RFC-3339 UTC while Frappe writes datetimes site-local, so the mistake this catches shows up as a CONSTANT offset the size of the site's timezone rather than as jitter, which is exactly how the Turnstile always-fail bug presented. Alarms above Chat Settings.clock_skew_alert_ms.
fields.label: Clock Skew (ms)
